verdict.summary: A draft single-click app installs on your own sandbox store within an hour, but draft apps only install on stores registered to your Developer Portal email. Letting any merchant connect requires becoming a BigCommerce partner and passing App Marketplace review, which charges a review and listing fee.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Register the draft app, set auth/load/uninstall callbacks to a public HTTPS tunnel, then install from Apps → My Apps → My Draft Apps on a sandbox store.

timeToProd.assumes: A public single-click app that any merchant can install, reading orders/products/customers; merchants can alternatively paste a store-level API token with no review, but that isn't OAuth.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Partner application approval (to get a Partner ID), then Marketplace team review and testing; you have 30 days to answer each round of feedback.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: BigCommerce doesn't publish review timelines. The range is our estimate for partner approval plus one or two review rounds.

verdict.cost: A review and listing fee is paid at Marketplace submission (amount not published in the docs we read). A free sandbox/trial store is enough for development.

prerequisites.item: A BigCommerce sandbox or trial store registered to the same email as your Developer Portal account
prerequisites.why: Draft apps can only be installed on stores registered to the Developer Portal email.

prerequisites.item: Public HTTPS URLs for the auth, load and uninstall callbacks
prerequisites.why: BigCommerce calls these over the internet and renders the app in a control-panel iframe; production callbacks must be fully qualified and served over TLS.
A Partner ID is required for Marketplace submission and is assigned after partner approval.

prerequisites.item: Complete listing assets, branded install page and support resources
prerequisites.why: All listing fields are required for approval, and the install callback must return styled, branded HTML rather than a blank page.

scopeTiers.impact: Works immediately on your own draft-app stores; standard Marketplace review for other merchants. Merchants must accept all requested scopes as a set.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Review is required for distribution, not per scope. Timeline is an estimate.

scopeTiers.impact: Same review path. Apps that create orders must set external_source to the app's ID.

Checkout Content scope triggers a security assessment; apps handling card data need a PCI review with an Attestation of Compliance. New externally built payment integrations are paused for the public Marketplace.
Apps configured with all scopes won't be approved for public listing.

steps.title: Create a sandbox store and Developer Portal account
steps.detail: Use the same email for both, so the store can install your draft apps.

steps.title: Choose minimal scopes
steps.detail: Pick read-only scopes like store_v2_orders_read_only and store_v2_products_read_only first; never select all scopes.

steps.title: Register the draft app
steps.detail: Developer Portal → Create an App → Technical: set Auth, Load and Uninstall callback URLs and scopes, then View Client ID to copy client_id and client_secret.

steps.title: Implement callbacks and token exchange
steps.detail: On GET /auth, POST code, scope, context, grant_type=authorization_code and redirect_uri (identical to the registered auth callback) to https://login.bigcommerce.com/oauth2/token before responding. Store the token against the store hash. Verify signed_payload_jwt on load and uninstall.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: JWT verification on load/uninstall is our summary of the separate callbacks article, not read in full.

steps.title: Install the draft on your sandbox store
steps.detail: Store control panel → Apps → My Apps → My Draft Apps → Install, and confirm the OAuth handshake completes.

steps.title: Apply to the partner program
steps.detail: Apply to become a BigCommerce Technology Partner to receive the Partner ID required for submission.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Partnership requirement is sourced; duration is our estimate.

steps.title: Draft the listing and meet requirements
steps.detail: Write listing copy, onboarding instructions and support content; check multi-user support, V3 endpoints, branded install HTML and Scripts API consent categories against the approval checklist.

steps.title: Pay the fee and submit
steps.detail: From the Apps overview choose Publish app…, add test account details for any third-party services, pay the review and listing fee, and submit.

steps.title: Marketplace review
steps.detail: The Marketplace team tests the app. Respond to feedback within 30 days, or the app is rejected for inactivity and a new fee is needed.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The 30-day response rule is sourced; review length is our estimate.

steps.title: Go live
steps.detail: Once approved, publish; listing changes can take up to 24 hours to appear.

agentCanDo: Build rate-limit-aware API clients using quota headers
Draft listing copy and onboarding docs
Check the app against the approval checklist
humanMustDo: Create the sandbox store and Developer Portal account
Pay the review and listing fee

blockers.symptom: A customer's store doesn't see your app under My Draft Apps
blockers.cause: Draft apps only install on stores registered to the same email as your Developer Portal account.
blockers.fix: Get Marketplace approval, or have the merchant create a store-level API account and give you the token.

blockers.symptom: Install fails or token exchange returns an error
blockers.cause: redirect_uri in the token request isn't identical to the auth callback in the app profile, or the callback isn't public HTTPS.
blockers.fix: Send the exact registered auth callback URL; update callbacks when your tunnel URL changes.

blockers.symptom: Stored access token stops working after a while
blockers.cause: Tokens are invalidated when the app's scopes change or the store owner's email changes; the merchant then re-accepts and you get a new auth callback.
blockers.fix: Handle repeat auth callbacks and overwrite the stored token for that store hash.

blockers.cause: All apps share a per-store quota (e.g. 150 requests per 30 s on Growth/Core); a 429 without rate-limit headers means high store load.
blockers.fix: Read X-Rate-Limit-Requests-Left and X-Rate-Limit-Time-Reset-Ms and back off.

blockers.cause: Apps configured with all scopes aren't approved for public listing.
blockers.fix: Request only the scopes your features use.

blockers.symptom: A store staff user can't install the app
blockers.cause: Reportedly only the store owner role can install apps.
blockers.fix: Ask the store owner to install.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: From a third-party integration guide, not BigCommerce docs.

nuances.text: App access tokens don't have a stated expiry (docs call them permanent or semi-permanent); there is no refresh token. They're replaced when scopes or the owner email change.
Rate limits are per store and shared across all apps: 60k/hour on Scale, 20k/hour on Growth and Core, with quotas refreshing every 30 seconds.
Merchants approve all requested scopes as a set; they can't choose a subset.
Marketplace apps must be multi-user enabled, and user tokens should be stored against the store hash, not the user's email.
Store-level API accounts (a static token a merchant creates in the control panel) are a no-review alternative for single-store integrations, but they're copy-paste credentials rather than OAuth.
The auth response includes account_uuid, the merchant's BigCommerce account that owns the store.
